Panchayats Act, 1958 established a two-tier

system of Village Panchayats and Panchayat

Unions.

The 73rd Constitutional Amendment

status, and the Tamil Nadu Panchayats Act,

1994 created a three-tier system with

directly elected members, reservations for

6.19.2. Medical Certification of Cause of Death (MCCD) and e-Mortality Software

Medical Certification of Cause of Death (MCCD), provided under Sections 10(2) and 10(3) of the Registration of Births and Deaths Act, 1969, is recorded in Form 4 for institutional deaths and Form 4A for non-institutional deaths. It is the primary source of cause-specific mortality data for public health planning and evidence-based policy formulation. To improve the quality and timeliness of mortality data, the web-based e-Mortality (e-Mor) module has been implemented.

398

Tamil Nadu has achieved 100% death registration since 2012. However, in 2024, medically certified causes of death were available for only 41% of registered deaths, highlighting the need to strengthen mortality surveillance.

To address this gap, the District Civil Registration System (CRS) Approach was piloted in Karur and Krishnagiri districts. The initiative integrates the WHO-recommended Verbal Autopsy methodology with digital technology to ascertain causes of community deaths lacking medical certification.

The pilot increased cause-of-death coverage from 41% to 98% in the pilot districts and reduced ill-defined causes of death from 46% to 13%, demonstrating substantial improvement in the completeness and quality of mortality data.

Based on these outcomes, the District CRS Approach, including Verbal Autopsy, is proposed to be expanded across Tamil Nadu in a phased manner by leveraging existing district-level infrastructure and strengthening technical capacity to generate high-quality mortality data for evidence-based planning, policy formulation and programme implementation.
